## What changed from v1

- **Logging after the fault.** v1 assumed both methods' remaining steps cancel. They don't: OutcomeServe still pays durable logging on every step after the fault, and the restart baseline does not. Adding that term cuts the mean absolute error of S over the nine cells from 2.37 s to 0.39 s. It also gets the sign right at 10% progress, where OutcomeServe measurably loses (−0.9 to −5.1 s).
- **Logging cost grows with the prefix.** Each CONTEXT_COMMITTED stores the full token prefix, so one step costs about 19 ms plus 22 µs per committed token: 0.07 s at 2K and 0.38 s at 16K. It is fitted to the fault-free Tier 1H cells. Leaving one prefix out predicts that prefix's H within +13% (2K), −2.5% (8K) and +3% (16K).
- **Task shape from the matrix.** The prefix grows 79 tokens per step (median of final minus initial prefix over 20 steps). The split between step prompt, call and tool result is still assumed; only the call length affects decode time.

## How to read it

- **The one-fault cells are out of sample.** The model is calibrated on the 11/03 spike's standalone cells, plus the logging cost fitted to the separate fault-free runs. None of the 360 one-fault runs enter the fit.
- **Fault → first new token** is predicted 0.3–0.8 s (1.5–3.8%) high in every cell. It is dominated by the replacement worker's ≈ 20 s start and is flat across prefixes, as measured.
- **Break-even q is much higher than v1 suggested.** With the measured H, OutcomeServe pays off at about q ≥ 0.45–0.52 at 50% progress and q ≥ 0.23–0.27 at 90%, and never at 10%. Measured S and H give the same values (for example 7.89 / (7.89 + 23.01) = 0.26 at 16K, 90%). v1's "a few percent" came from a 0.5 s H measured on a laptop with a constant per-step cost.
- **The lever is the log format, not recovery.** Recovery itself is cheap and well predicted. The saving is eaten by writing the full prefix on every step. Storing only each step's new tokens would make the per-step cost nearly flat. In the model, logging only the ~79 new tokens per step cuts H at 16K from 7.9 s to about 0.4 s and break-even q at 16K, 90% from about 0.26 to about 0.02. This is a design implication for future work, not something we measured.

## Limits

- One GPU, inference-process restart, APC off, 20-step tasks, at most one fault per task. Runner-domain and APC-on predictions remain spike-only checks.
- Restart's tool reset time is taken as 0. The supervisor records it (TOOL_RESET_* events), but runs.csv does not; it is milliseconds against seconds of S.
- q is an assumed probability of one fault per task, not a measured crash rate (plan section 6).
